title: Software Publishers
why: SSDF develops, licenses, and publishes software across AMAIMA, MNEMOS, StackDesk, Genesis Engine, BasisGuard, and Digital Commerce.
deliverable: Licensed software, platform components, and published digital products.
restrictions: License scope and export/ITAR classification evaluated per solicitation.

title: Custom Computer Programming Services
why: SSDF and AMAIMA perform custom development of cryptographic, workflow, and operational software.
deliverable: Application code, integrations, and defined software deliverables.
restrictions: Place of performance, security, and IP terms are solicitation-specific.

title: Computer Systems Design Services
why: Architecture, systems integration, and cryptographic infrastructure design are core SSDF work.
deliverable: Architecture, integration, and system-design artifacts.
restrictions: Classified or CUI work requires matching facility and personnel conditions.

title: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services
why: Claimed only where SSDF directly provides the applicable hosting, processing, or infrastructure service.
deliverable: Compute, data processing, or hosted platform services actually operated by SSDF.
restrictions: Not a claim of hyperscale data-center ownership. Scope limited to services SSDF directly provides.

title: IT and Telecom — Application Development Software, Perpetual License Software
why: SSDF licenses application-development software components from its portfolio.
deliverable: Perpetual software license and associated documentation.
restrictions: License grant, maintenance, and audit rights are contract-specific.

title: IT and Telecom — Business Application Software, Perpetual License Software
why: Business-application software (commerce, evidence, planning, production) is published by SSDF.
deliverable: Perpetual business-application license.
restrictions: Use restrictions and environment follow the license and solicitation.

title: IT and Telecom — Service Delivery Management
why: SSDF operates service-delivery and control-plane software for its platforms and federal execution layer.
deliverable: Service-delivery management software or managed operation of that layer.
restrictions: Does not imply ownership of the customer’s ITSM stack.

title: Business Application / Application Development Support Services — Labor
why: Labor for application development and support is a direct SSDF engagement model (T&M or fixed-price).
deliverable: Development and support labor against a statement of work.
restrictions: Labor categories, clearances, and place of performance are solicitation-specific.

title: Business Application / Application Development Software as a Service
why: Platform services (TaaS, commerce, evidence, production OS) are delivered as software-as-a-service.
deliverable: SaaS access, usage tiers, and operational support.
restrictions: FedRAMP and agency ATO are acquired per engagement, not claimed as already held.

title: High Performance Computing Support Services — Labor
why: FHE / HEXL cryptographic compute is HPC-class work. Labor is assembled against the requirement.
deliverable: HPC support labor for cryptographic and scientific compute.
restrictions: Facility, hardware, and clearance conditions evaluated per opportunity.

title: Compute Support Services, Non-HPC — Labor
why: Non-HPC compute support for SSDF-operated platforms and customer deployments.
deliverable: Compute support labor.
restrictions: Scope limited to environments SSDF is contracted to operate or support.

title: Compute as a Service — Mainframe / Servers
why: Sovereign and domestic-kernel compute can be offered as a service where SSDF operates the stack.
deliverable: Contracted compute capacity under SSDF control.
restrictions: Not a claim of mainframe ownership. Partnered capacity disclosed when used.

title: Data Center Support Services — Labor
why: Labor for data-center support where SSDF is contracted to operate or oversee the environment.
deliverable: Data-center support labor.
restrictions: Physical facility access, union, and clearance rules are solicitation-specific.

title: Data Center as a Service
why: Sovereign deployment can include data-center-as-a-service structures using qualified facilities.
deliverable: Hosted / sovereign data-center service under contract.
restrictions: SSDF does not claim to own a national data-center fleet.

title: Service Delivery Support Services / ITSM / Operations Center / Project-PM — Labor
why: Program, operations-center, and service-delivery labor is a native SSDF control-plane function.
deliverable: ITSM, ops-center, and project-management labor.
restrictions: On-site vs remote and clearance conditions follow the solicitation.

title: End User / Help Desk / Workspace / Productivity Tools — Labor
why: End-user support can be assembled through qualified labor under SSDF control.
deliverable: Help-desk and workspace support labor.
restrictions: Limitations on subcontracting and wage determinations apply when imposed.

title: Mobile Device Support Services — Labor
why: Mobile-device support is a fulfillment lane, not a standing internal help desk.
deliverable: Mobile-device support labor.
restrictions: MDM, device ownership, and privacy rules are solicitation-specific.

title: End User as a Service
why: EUaaS is bid only when SSDF can assemble the managed-workspace stack under contract.
deliverable: Managed end-user environment.
restrictions: Device, identity, and network boundaries must be specified in the solicitation.

title: Mobile Device as a Service
why: MDaaS is a contract-specific fulfillment structure, not a standing carrier-style device fleet.
deliverable: Managed mobile-device service.
restrictions: Supply-chain and domestic-sourcing rules evaluated per opportunity.

title: Platform Support Services — Database / Mainframe / Middleware — Labor
why: Platform, database, and middleware support for SSDF-built cryptographic and operational stacks.
deliverable: Platform support labor.
restrictions: Mainframe labor is bid only where the requirement matches actual capability.

title: Platform as a Service — Database / Mainframe / Middleware
why: AMAIMA platform components can be delivered as PaaS for sovereign and enterprise deployments.
deliverable: Managed platform service.
restrictions: Not a generic AWS-style PaaS catalog. Scope is SSDF/AMAIMA platform components.

title: Security and Compliance Support Services — Labor
why: Cryptographic, compliance, and verification labor is a demonstrated AMAIMA/BasisGuard capability.
deliverable: Security and compliance support labor, architecture, and review.
restrictions: Does not claim FedRAMP authorization already in hand.

title: Security and Compliance as a Service
capability: Security and compliance as a service
why: TaaS and cryptographic verification are production services, not documentation overlay.
deliverable: Verification, attestation, and compliance services on a usage or subscription basis.
restrictions: Service boundary and evidence standard defined in the SOW.

title: Network Support Services — Labor
why: Network architecture and support for sovereign and platform deployments.
deliverable: Network support labor.
restrictions: Not a claim of nationwide NOC staffing.

title: Network as a Service
why: NaaS is offered where SSDF operates or orchestrates the network layer of a contracted deployment.
deliverable: Managed network service under contract.
restrictions: Not a telecommunications common-carrier offering.

title: Network: Satellite Communications and Telecom Access Services
why: AMAIMA implements independent multi-source satellite trust attestation (Galileo OSNMA, GPS, GLONASS) and related sovereign communications architecture. Retained as a serious capability candidate — not as a claim that SSDF is a commercial satellite carrier.
deliverable: Satellite-trust attestation, related telecom-access architecture, and contracted communications services that match the actual technical implementation.
restrictions: Evaluate against the exact technical implementation and solicitation. Do not interpret as conventional carrier or SATCOM fleet ownership.

title: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)
why: AMAIMA’s cryptographic, AI, quantum-classical, verification, and sovereign-infrastructure work is applied and experimental R&D.
deliverable: Research, prototypes, experimental development, and technical reports.
restrictions: Nanotechnology and biotechnology are excluded by the NAICS definition used here.

title: National Defense R&D Services — DoD — Military — Basic Research
why: Cryptographic and computational research can support basic-research vehicles where the requirement matches.
deliverable: Basic-research output under a defense R&D vehicle.
restrictions: Security, publication, and ITAR/EAR restrictions control. Bid only against matching requirements.

title: National Defense R&D Services — DoD — Military — Applied Research
why: Applied cryptographic AI, verification, and quantum-classical routing are demonstrated AMAIMA work.
deliverable: Applied-research artifacts and prototypes.
restrictions: Facility and personnel security must match the solicitation.

title: National Defense R&D Services — DoD — Military — Experimental Development
why: Production FHE, PQ signing, and sovereign-ledger infrastructure is experimental development already running.
deliverable: Experimental systems, test articles, and development evidence.
restrictions: Does not claim prior DoD program-of-record past performance.

title: Professional Engineering / Technical Support
why: Systems architecture, cryptographic engineering, and technical support are native professional services.
deliverable: Engineering and technical support labor and artifacts.
restrictions: PE licensure is obtained per jurisdiction when the solicitation requires it.

title: Operations Research / Quantitative Analysis
why: Quantitative analysis, evolutionary search, and opportunity economics are operating capabilities.
deliverable: Analysis, models, and research memoranda.
restrictions: Not a claim of federally certified OR past performance.

title: Other Accounting Services
why: Retained only where the corresponding service is actually offered (evidence, position records, management accounting support).
deliverable: Accounting-related services that SSDF actually performs.
restrictions: Not a CPA-firm representation. Bid only when the service is actually offered.

title: Professional Program Management / Support
why: SSDF’s prime-contractor model is a program and control layer over execution.
deliverable: Program management and professional support.
restrictions: PMP or equivalent credentials acquired when a solicitation requires them.

title: Professional Market Research / Public Opinion
why: Retained only where an actual qualifying research service is offered.
deliverable: Market or opinion research that SSDF actually contracts to deliver.
restrictions: Conditional. Not a standing polling house.

title: Management Data Collection
why: Evidence, ledgers, and operational data collection are native to SSDF platforms.
deliverable: Collected, attested management data.
restrictions: Privacy, CUI, and records rules follow the solicitation.

title: Management Accounting
why: Management accounting is offered where SSDF actually performs the service.
deliverable: Management-accounting artifacts and support.
restrictions: Not audited financial-statement services unless separately contracted and qualified.

title: Management Auditing
why: Verification and evidence review can constitute management-auditing support when that is the actual service.
deliverable: Audit-support and verification work.
restrictions: Not a PCAOB audit firm. Bid only for matching scopes.

title: Management Logistics Support
why: SSDF Transportation provides the technology and operational control layer for logistics support.
deliverable: Logistics coordination, evidence, and management support.
restrictions: Does not automatically make SSDF the freight carrier.

title: Contract / Procurement / Acquisition Support
why: The Federal Opportunity Engine is acquisition-support machinery: discover, qualify, price, resource.
deliverable: Acquisition-support analysis and program assistance.
restrictions: Organizational conflict of interest reviewed per solicitation.

title: Process, Physical Distribution, and Logistics Consulting Services
why: Consulting on process, distribution, and logistics is offered where actually provided.
deliverable: Logistics consulting and control-plane design.
restrictions: Consulting is not operating authority as a carrier or broker.

title: Transportation / Travel / Relocation — Transportation: Other
why: Transportation opportunities are evaluated for carrier, broker, equipment, insurance, and licensing before any bid.
deliverable: Transportation-related services SSDF is authorized to perform on that contract.
restrictions: SSDF does not represent itself as the actual transportation carrier simply because it operates dispatch infrastructure.

title: Facilities Support Services
why: Prime-plus-fulfillment lane. SSDF may organize qualified workforce and vendors under contract.
deliverable: Facilities support performed through permitted execution partners under SSDF control.
restrictions: Limitations on subcontracting, wage determinations, and licensing apply when imposed.

title: Janitorial Services
why: Potential fulfillment category — not a claim of a standing internal janitorial workforce.
deliverable: Janitorial services via qualified fulfillment under SSDF prime.
restrictions: SCA, union, and security-escort rules follow the solicitation.

title: Landscaping Services
why: Potential fulfillment category under the prime-plus-fulfillment model.
deliverable: Landscaping / groundskeeping via qualified fulfillment.
restrictions: Licensing, equipment, and place-of-performance conditions apply.

title: Other Services to Buildings and Dwellings
why: Catch-all building-services lane for qualified fulfillment where the solicitation permits.
deliverable: Specified building services under SSDF control.
restrictions: Trade licensing evaluated per task.

title: Remediation Services
why: Disaster and facilities remediation may be assembled through qualified specialized vendors.
deliverable: Remediation performed by qualified resources under SSDF prime.
restrictions: Environmental licenses, bonding, and OSHA rules are mandatory gates.

title: All Other Miscellaneous Waste Management Services
why: Waste and cleanup support for disaster and facilities work, via qualified vendors.
deliverable: Specified waste-management services.
restrictions: Hauler permits and disposal-facility rules are solicitation-specific.

title: Housekeeping — Custodial / Janitorial
why: Federal housekeeping lane corresponding to janitorial fulfillment.
deliverable: Custodial services under SSDF prime.
restrictions: Not a representation that SSDF currently employs the entire trade workforce.

title: Housekeeping — Trash / Garbage Collection
why: Fulfillment lane for collection services where permitted.
deliverable: Collection services via qualified vendors.
restrictions: Local franchise and permit rules may bar performance.

title: Housekeeping — Guard
why: Guard services only through licensed security resources under contract.
deliverable: Guard services via licensed fulfillment.
restrictions: State guard licensing, weapons, and suitability investigations are hard gates.

title: Housekeeping — Landscaping / Groundskeeping
why: Groundskeeping fulfillment under the prime-plus-fulfillment model.
deliverable: Landscaping and groundskeeping via qualified resources.
restrictions: Equipment, chemicals, and wage rules follow the solicitation.

title: Employment Placement Agencies
why: Capability-building lane — not a representation that SSDF currently operates a conventional staffing agency.
deliverable: Placement services if and when the contract structure and licensing permit.
restrictions: State employment-agency licensing and FLSA status are evaluated before any bid.

title: Temporary Help Services
why: Workforce is evaluated by labor category, place of performance, wage, licensing, and subcontracting limits.
deliverable: Temporary help under a contract-specific structure.
restrictions: SSDF does not claim to currently operate a conventional staffing agency.
